original_value: At present, to improve the accuracy and performance for personalized recommendation in mobile wireless networks, deep learning has been widely concerned and employed with social and mobile trajectory big data. However, it is still challenging to implement increasingly complex personalized recommendation applications over big data. In view of this challenge, a hybrid recommendation framework, i.e., deep CNN-assisted personalized recommendation, named DCAPR, is proposed for mobile users. Technically, DCAPR integrates multisource heterogeneous data through convolutional neural network, as well as inputs various features, including image features, text semantic features, and mobile social user trajectories, to construct a deep prediction model. Specifically, we acquire the location information and moving trajectory sequence in the mobile wireless network first. Then, the similarity of users is calculated according to the sequence of moving trajectories to pick the neighboring users. Furthermore, we recommend the potential visiting locations for mobile users through the deep learning CNN network with the social and mobile trajectory big data. Finally, a real-word large-scale dataset, collected from Gowalla, is leveraged to verify the accuracy and effectiveness of our proposed DCAPR model.

result.paraphrase: To improve the accuracy and efficiency of personalized recommendation in mobile wireless networks, deep learning has been widely studied and applied to social and mobile trajectory big data. Yet implementing increasingly complex personalized recommendation applications on big data remains challenging. To address this, we propose a hybrid recommendation framework for mobile users called DCAPR, a deep CNN-assisted personalized recommendation method. DCAPR uses a convolutional neural network to fuse multisource heterogeneous data and incorporates image features, text semantic features, and mobile social user trajectories to build a deep prediction model. First, we obtain location information and moving trajectory sequences in the mobile wireless network. Next, user similarity is computed from the trajectory sequences to select neighboring users. Then, potential visiting locations for mobile users are recommended through a deep learning CNN network using social and mobile trajectory big data. Finally, a real-world large-scale dataset collected from Gowalla is used to validate the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed DCAPR model.
